summary_en: This Phase II study tests high dose radiation therapy given with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in patients with PD-L1 positive metastatic triple negative breast cancer. Radiation is given once every other day for 3 doses, pembrolizumab is given by IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and patients also receive one of three chemotherapy options: nab-paclitaxel or paclitaxel IV on days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle, or carboplatin and gemcitabine IV on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is Phase II.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa la radioterapia de dosis alta administrada junto con pembrolizumab y quimioterapia en pacientes con cáncer de mama triple negativo metastásico con PD-L1 positivo. La radioterapia se administra una vez cada dos días en 3 dosis, el pembrolizumab se administra por vía IV el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y los pacientes también reciben una de tres opciones de quimioterapia: nab-paclitaxel o paclitaxel IV los días 1, 8 y 15 de cada ciclo, o carboplatino y gemcitabina IV los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 21 días. El resultado principal del estudio no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Biopsy-proven metastatic PD-L1 positive triple negative breast cancer with at least 2 measurable metastatic sites on imaging.
PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or higher by the Dako 22c3 assay.
At least 1 metastatic site that can be treated with high dose radiotherapy.
Age 18 years or older, with ECOG performance status 0-2 or Karnofsky 60% or higher.
ER and PR negative (10% or fewer cells) and HER2 negative by the stated tests.
not_for: Prior chemotherapy or targeted therapy for metastatic triple negative breast cancer before starting this combination.
Previous radiation to the metastases that would be treated on this study.
Untreated brain or central nervous system disease.
Uncontrolled pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or ascites.
Autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment, or HIV with CD4 count below 200 cells/microliter.
